newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power higher in line with natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power higher in line with natgas.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West continued to climb amid below-normal temperatures in the Northwest and sharply higher spot natural gas prices, market sources said Wednesday.
"The market is still strong, but I expect things to turn around by the end of the week," said one Arizona trader.
He noted that recent demand from storm-battered Northwest utilities will likely taper off by then.
But natural gas prices, spurred by storage-related demand throughout the U.S., have continued to climb.
Traders said this week's Northwest rainfall will boost hydroelectric output, but prices are unlikely to fall much below the cost of gas generation.

"All they (sellers of hydropower) have to do is price it 50 cents or $1.00 under gas costs," said a Canadian trader. He added that much colder than normal temperatures in Alberta are likely to draw local supplies of electricity as well as natural gas.
"A lot of paper and options are being closed out," said another market source. "This is creating physical demand for gas in the prompt months."
Next-day firm, on-peak power at the California-Oregon border (COB) was last quoted $31.00-33.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from $29.00-30.00 on Tuesday. Off-peak COB was quoted $18.00-19.00.
Next-day firm, on-peak power at Mid-Columbia was last quoted $32.00-34.00, while off-peak was quoted $18.50-21.00.
Palo Verde next-day firm, on-peak power was quoted $26.00-28.00 per MWh, up from from Tuesday. Off-peak Palo Verde was quoted at $14.00-15.00.
Four Corners firm, on-peak power was quoted at $27.00-28.00, while off-peak was at $14.50-15.50.
